h2: One Skill, Three Timers, and a Score You Should Not Trust
lede: Psi training apps live in an awkward position: the claim underneath them is weak, the practice underneath them is legitimate, and the score the app displays is the one part that does not measure anything. Almost every training scheme that produces a number is scoring familiarity with the apparatus. The parts that carry weight are unglamorous: one narrow task, a fixed daily slot, and a record that is written before the guess rather than after. What follows is how to use one of these apps so that the first month produces something you can keep, and what to do with the score in the meantime.

sections.h3: The claim underneath, and the part that is real
p: The claim is that repeated guessing against shuffled symbols trains a faculty. There is a long literature on this and almost none of it survives contact with a good design, which is a problem that has been analysed thoroughly in this library under [the statistics of the standard deck](the-mind-science-of-practice-why-does-magic-work-placeb-7) and [the version that starts from expectancy](the-mind-science-of-practice-why-does-magic-work-placebo). The finding that does not need a stake in the argument is that the rig is not guessing, and a weak decline in guessing rate over repeated exposure is a training result in a laboratory, not a supernormal ability.

The part that is real is narrower and more useful. Attention held flat for four minutes, daily, is a trainable capacity with a large literature behind it, and it does not need the deck to be worth doing. [The autonomic measurement side of the claim](the-mind-science-of-practice-why-does-magic-work-placeb-11) is the honest half, and [plasticity as a description rather than a promise](meditacion-neuroplasticidad-why-does-magic-work-placebo) is the right register for the month-one expectation. If you want the sceptical version of the whole question, [can anyone learn this at all](can-anyone-learn-esp-the-science-says-maybe) is the entry point.

sections.h3: Why a score goes up when nothing improves
p: A percentage that climbs is the expected consequence of three things happening at once: you memorise the rig, you learn to feel the tell, and you get better at guessing under low stakes. None of those is the faculty the app claims to be building, and the number will improve whether or not anything else does. [Thirty days of score keeping](zener-training-30-day-score-journey) is the more useful record, and [a proper daily schedule](best-esp-training-schedule-daily-psi-practice) is the practical alternative to chasing a figure.

The fix is not to distrust the score but to demote it. Log it, do not aim at it. A schedule that produces a rising number is fine; a schedule aimed at producing one produces a rising number whatever happens, which is a false-positive generator by construction. [Training intuition against the science](can-you-train-intuition-science-esp-methods) is the careful version of the same point.

sections.h3: The three timers, and why one task
p: A workable arrangement is unglamorous: one task repeated, three sessions a day, each a few minutes. The task should be narrow enough that you are not choosing during it, and it should not be the task you most want to succeed at, because wanting to succeed is the one variable that ruins the measurement. [The daily practice and the schedule](best-esp-training-schedule-daily-psi-practice) sets out the arrangement in more detail.

The reason for one task is that it removes the decision, and the decision is what most training schemes are actually measuring. A session where you spend the first ninety seconds deciding what to do is a session about deciding. [The gnosis exercise in four questions](gnosis-protocol-four-questions) is a version of the same discipline in a different domain, and it is worth reading because it makes the point about pre-committed aims rather than open-ended effort.

Most apps of this kind ship three modes and differ on what they ask you to hold. One asks for a symbol, one for a picture, one for a feeling. The choice is worth making deliberately because it changes what your log will look like, and none of the three is better in the abstract. Symbols give you a clean hit rate and a low ceiling. Pictures give you a richer record and no score at all. Feelings give you the most usable training signal and the least transferable one.

The [psychonaut material on altered states](psychonautics-and-altered-states-psychonautics-guide-guide) is the wider context for why this kind of training appeals to people who are also interested in the harder end of the practice, and [the psychology of the altered state itself](the-mind-science-of-practice-why-does-magic-work-placeb-12) is the more careful treatment. Whichever mode you pick, the sensible move is to run one for a full month before changing it, because switching modes resets the log.

Getting better at this, in whatever sense of the word you end up using, is mostly a matter of doing it badly in front of a record. The ladder is short: first you guess confidently and get it wrong, then you guess and notice you were wrong, then you guess and can say why, then you notice the state before the guess rather than after. Most people stop on the second rung and conclude the method is defective.

[Reprogramming your brain as a practice](neural-grimoire-reprogramming-your-brain-chaos-magic) is the version of that ladder with more ambition attached, and it is worth reading for the framing rather than for the promises. [This app's review](psi-gym-app-review) is more measured than the marketing and worth your time before you pay for anything.

sections.h3: What the first month actually delivers
p: In month one the objective is not a result. It is a habit that survives a week you did not want to practise, and a log with enough entries that month two has something to compare against. That is the whole target, and it is achievable by almost anyone who reads the schedule and does it.

If the aim is gnosis rather than a deck, the first month has a different shape and the [four-question protocol](gnosis-protocol-four-questions) is the instrument for it. The gnosis family in this library covers the same ground at more length, including [the structure of the claim](abraxas-what-is-gnosis-chaos-magic), [where the confirmation engine sits](advoluntrapraem-what-is-gnosis-chaos-magic), and [the first-timer's version](alfa-what-is-gnosis-chaos-magic), which is the one to read if you have never kept a record before.

sections.h3: What the app is training, and what it is only measuring
p: Read the app as a motor drill rather than a test. The daily score moves for at least three reasons that have nothing to do with knowing anything: you memorised the order of the rig, you learned to feel for the tell, and you got better at guessing. Only the third is even arguably skill, and it is a real one, but it is not the one the app claims. The longer treatment of that gap is in [Can anyone learn ESP](can-anyone-learn-esp-the-science-says-maybe) and in [how the mind keeps a practice honest](abraxas-what-is-gnosis-chaos-magic), which is the same epistemological problem wearing different clothes.

The training schedule is the part of the product that carries the claim, and it is worth reading as a written method rather than as a feature list. [The best daily ESP schedule](best-esp-training-schedule-daily-psi-practice) and [thirty days of scored practice](zener-training-30-day-score-journey) both set out a shape you could reproduce on paper with a deck, which is the honest test of whether you need the app at all. If you want the statistical background behind the deck itself, [what a Zener card is and where the number comes from](what-is-a-zener-card-definition-history-statistics) is the shortest route.

sections.h3: The four questions the app never asks
p: Does the score change when the answer changes, or only when the guessing changes? Could a colleague with a different deck have scored the same? What was the base rate on the day before you started? Would you have noticed a bad week? The [gnosis protocol in four questions](gnosis-protocol-four-questions) is the shortest written form of those, and [belief as a tool rather than a cause](gnosis-belief-and-paradigm-shift-what-is-gnosis-chaos-m-3) is the longer version. [Meditation and neuroplasticity](meditacion-neuroplasticidad-why-does-magic-work-placebo) covers the training half of the question, and [the four questions protocol for clarity workings](gnosis-protocol-four-questions) shows the same four questions applied to a decision rather than a card.

If the honest answer to the base-rate question is that you never counted one, the fix is a deck and a notebook rather than an app. [Rune practice as the workable alternative](learning-to-read-runes-daily-practice) and [intuition as a trainable faculty](can-you-train-intuition-science-esp-methods) both describe what a measurement-led practice looks like when you build it from scratch.

sections.h3: What the training is a sample of
p: Scores, timers and streak counters all look like progress and none of them is the thing being trained.
